title: UK fixed-income market recommended closed all day for the Boxing Day substitute bank holiday — with New York trading a full session
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule ('Holiday Schedule'), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 298,926 bytes) and parsed card-by-card (h3 name / date / note) with region attribution fixed to the page's own 'U.S. / U.K. / Japan Holiday Recommendations' <h2> headings, then re-parsed independently out of the page's embedded Next.js flight payload (121 cards across all six panels) by this session. The U.K. 2026 panel's 17th card reads exactly ['Boxing Day (Substitute)', 'Monday, December 28, 2026'] with NO early-close note attached — the full-closure shape, distinct from the 'Early Close' entries elsewhere on the same page. The causing holiday is independently statutory: gov.uk/bank-holidays.json (HTTP 200, 22,207 bytes, the England-and-Wales division) lists '2026-12-28 | Boxing Day | Substitute day', 2026-12-26 falling on a Saturday. Cross-checked the same day against the page's U.S. panel, which carries NO 2026-12-28 card at all — its December entries are the 12-24 early close, the 12-25 closure and the 12-31 early close — so the recommended US fixed-income tape runs a full session while London is dark. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to the four sifma-* entries already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an industry trade association's recommended schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and SIFMA's own page states its schedule is a recommendation ('On behalf of financial markets participants, SIFMA recommends a holiday schedule for financial markets in the U.S., U.K. and Japan') rather than a market-wide halt each firm is bound by.
notes: DISCOVERED during the sifma-japan-early-close-2026-12-28 initial research (2026-09-05). WHY IT EARNS A ROW: it is the CAUSE of the Japan-panel entry already tracked on this date. SIFMA's page states its scope verbatim — 'All SIFMA holiday recommendations apply to the trading of U.S. dollar-denominated government securities, mortgage- and asset-backed securities, over-the-counter investment-grade and high-yield corporate bonds, municipal bonds and secondary money market trading in bankers' acceptances, commercial paper and Yankee and Euro certificates of deposit' — so the three regional panels are three TIME ZONES of one US-dollar market, not three asset classes. On 2026-12-28 that market sits in three different states at once: London recommended fully closed (this entry), Tokyo recommended closed early at 15:00 JST (sifma-japan-early-close-2026-12-28), New York running a normal session. That is the exact INVERSE of the triple three days later on 2026-12-31, where the US closes early, Tokyo is fully dark and the UK is normal (sifma-bond-early-close-2026-12-31, jpx-market-closure-2026-12-31). This is the FIRST U.K.-panel entry on this calendar; the four existing sifma-* entries are three US-panel and one Japan-panel. IMPACT LOW: a recommended closure in a foreign fixed-income market moves nothing by itself, no house playbook is calendar-, holiday- or rates-keyed (docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md grepped this session for 'holiday|jpx|tokyo|nikkei|closure|year-end|new year|jgb|gilt|boxing|sifma': zero hits in both), and this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol or gilt instrument. It changes who is at a desk, not what anything is worth. MEASURED, not assumed: across 244 Tokyo sessions since 1990 with London shut (detector = a weekday with an ^N225 bar and no ^FTSE bar, validated 51/52 precision and 51/51 recall against gov.uk's statutory list for 2019+), the Nikkei's mean |close-to-close| runs 0.964% against 1.008% for an ordinary session — Welch t = -0.78, i.e. no measurable footprint; on the exact London-shut/New-York-open configuration this date produces, 0.997% at t = -0.16. HONEST LIMIT: SIFMA's 2027 U.K. panel gives this same holiday a 'None' recommendation while gov.uk dates a 2027-12-28 substitute, and its 2027 U.K. Christmas card reads 'Friday, December 24, 2027' rather than gov.uk's Monday substitute — so the 2027 year-end panel is either genuinely year-by-year or simply unfinished, and this entry is filed on the 2026 panel alone, which carries no tentative flag. It is a recommendation to member firms, NOT an exchange closure; the London Stock Exchange's own calendar was not fetched this session and nothing is asserted about equity hours.
